raw_segments.text: Antonio, but little. I am armed and well-propar'd. Give me your hand, Bassanio. Fair you well,
grieve not that I am fallen to this for you, for herein fortune shows herself more kind
than is her custom. It is still her use to let the wretched man outlive his wealth, to
view with hollow eye and wrinkled brow an age of poverty, from which lingering penance
of such misery doth she cut me off.
Commend me to your honorable wife. Tell her the process of Antonio's end. Say how I loved you,
speak me fair in death. And when the tale is told, bid her be judged whether Bassanio had
not once a love. Repent but you that you shall lose your friend, and he repents not that he
pays your debt. For if the Jew do cut but deep enough, I'll pay it instantly with all my heart.
